Ransomware Attack Disrupts Key Madagascar Agriculture Firms, Halts Operations

A major ransomware attack has struck several leading agriculture firms in Madagascar, causing widespread disruption to operations across the sector. The cyber assault, which began late Tuesday night, has encrypted critical IT systems at multiple crop production and agro-processing sites, leaving management teams scrambling to contain the fallout.

According to sector sources, the attack has primarily targeted companies in the Alaotra-Mangoro and Sofia regions, both vital hubs for Madagascar’s rice and vanilla production. “We have not been able to access our planting schedules, machinery controls, or payroll systems,” said Marie Raharisoa, operations manager at SoaAgriculture Group. “This is having a direct impact on our ability to manage field operations and process crops.”

The National Federation of Agricultural Enterprises (FNEA) reports that at least eight major firms have been affected, with more expected to confirm breaches as investigations continue. Several packing and storage facilities have suspended activity, and thousands of workers have been sent home pending restoration of IT systems. “Our members are deeply concerned about the immediate loss of productivity and the risk of crop spoilage,” said FNEA spokesperson Jean-Luc Ramanantsoa.

The attackers are demanding payment in cryptocurrency to unlock the affected systems. While no company has publicly confirmed paying the ransom, industry experts warn the disruption could escalate if systems are not restored soon. “The timing is especially damaging, as this is the peak export season for vanilla and lychee,” noted agricultural analyst Hanitra Rasoamanana. “Any prolonged shutdown will affect revenues and worker livelihoods.”

Field managers report that automated irrigation and climate control systems have also been rendered inoperable at some sites, raising concerns about crop health. “We are reverting to manual methods where possible, but this is not sustainable,” said a site supervisor at Malagasy Harvest Ltd.

Authorities and private sector cybersecurity teams are working to contain the breach, but no timeline has been given for full recovery. Meanwhile, union representatives are urging companies to ensure prompt wage payments for affected workers and prioritize system restoration. The industry remains on high alert as the situation develops.
